findings.title: join() skips terminate when the deadline is already spent
findings.body: SpanFlusher.join() gives the entire timeout to next_step.join(), then breaks out of the process loop as soon as remaining_time <= 0, before process.terminate(). The previous single-process join always called terminate() after the wait, even if the deadline had passed. Arroyo shutdown/rebalance uses a finite join timeout, so after this change every flusher process is left running. Those processes are only daemonized, not stopped, and the consumer process stays alive across rebalance, so the old flushers keep calling flush_segments/produce on the same Redis shards as the replacement consumer. That yields duplicate buffered-segments and concurrent Redis expiry/delete races.

findings.title: Flusher metric tags are a joined shard list
findings.body: Produce/wait timers tag metrics with shard_tag = ",".join(all shards owned by that process). --flusher-processes defaults to 1, so the common case is one process for every assigned partition and a single tag value like "0,1,2,...,N". That value changes with every assignment, blows past typical tag-length limits (metrics get dropped), and is a different key on the wait timer ("shards") than on the produce timer ("shard"). Per-shard flusher health and latency dashboards will not work.

findings.title: Added flusher wait is a no-op under the sleep patch
findings.body: test_basic monkeypatches time.sleep to a no-op, then calls time.sleep(0.1) to let the flusher observe the drift update before join(). That call is the patched no-op, so it does not yield. join() sets stopped immediately; if the flusher thread has not yet run flush_segments with drift 9000, the segment is never produced and the assertion on messages fails intermittently. The new test does not actually cover the race it was added for.
